## ❓ 1. Why this Book

> Knowing what a service *does* is not the same as knowing *when* to choose it — and what you must be prepared to defend once you have.

This is a companion to [**Foundational Questions. Visual Answers. Mastering AWS Fundamentals**](https://senthilkumarm1901.github.io/learn_by_blogging/aws_cloud_technical_essentials/). That book builds the fundamentals, chapter by chapter: security, compute, networking, storage, databases, monitoring, optimization. This book assumes those fundamentals and asks a harder question: given a real customer's requirements, how do you *combine* those building blocks into one architecture — and justify the services you rejected?

A companion blog post walks through this same way of thinking end to end: [**Thinking like a Cloud Architect**](https://senthilkumarm1901.github.io/learn_by_blogging/posts/cloud_architect/cloud_architect.html).

---

## 📝 2. What this book covers

Every chapter follows the same workflow: **requirements → architectural drivers → candidate services → trade-offs → decision → justified rejections.**

### 🧩 [**10. Architecting a Serverless Web Backend**](10-architecting-serverless-backend-solution-in-aws.html)

A monolithic, on-prem order service must become an auto-scaling, decoupled, serverless backend — deciding how clients get in, what runs the business logic, and where state lives.

### 📊 [**11. Serverless Data Analytics**](11-serverless-data-analytics.html)

Static S3-hosted menus need a clickstream pipeline bolted on — turning a one-off request into a recurring **ingest → store → query → visualise** data pipeline.

### 🔗 [**12. Hybrid, Container-Based Workloads**](12-hybrid-container-workloads.html)

Half a company's workloads stay on-premises, half move to AWS — connecting the two, keeping containers portable, and migrating a database with near-zero downtime.

### 🏛️ [**13. Account Governance and Multi-Account Management**](13-multi-account-strategies.html)

A single, unmanaged AWS account has to become a governed multi-account structure — with automatic provisioning, single sign-on, central logging and guardrails.

### 🎯 [**14. Capstone: Decoupled App + EMR Analytics**](14-capstone-decoupled-app-and-emr-analytics.html)

One customer, two workloads at once: decoupling a three-tier app and re-platforming a Hadoop estate onto Amazon EMR — reusing the patterns from Chapters 10-12 together.
